incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: metrics-pipeline > log-ingest-consumer-lag (severity: P1) - PagerDuty #PD-22183 - https://pagerduty.local/PD-22183

incident-bot: details: consumer group 'log-ingest-group' lag > 250k msgs for topic 'raw-logs' in us-west-2 for > 5m. autoscroll policy: page primary oncall, escalate to sec after 2m.

sre_oncall_alex: ack - I'm on it. looking at consumer group lag in Kafka, will check consumer pods and CPU. :wave:

maria: saw a spike around 02:14 UTC, likely from increased traffic from batch jobs. dashboards show write-through to raw-logs up ~3x.

kai: pinging the autoscaler for log-consumer: `kubectl get hpa -n ingest log-consumer -o yaml`

sre_oncall_alex: running quick consumer lag check:
```bash
# kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-01:9092 --describe --group log-ingest-group | grep raw-logs
TOPIC         PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
raw-logs      0          1234500         1500000         265000  consumer-7
raw-logs      1          1234000         1501000         267000  consumer-8
```

sre_oncall_alex: lag ~265k per partition, consumer pods at 60% CPU across the board. autoscaler shows desired=3, current=3. Not scaling up automatically.

dave: looks like HPA target CPU is 75%. Might need to temporarily spin up extra replicas. I can patch deployment to force scale.

emma: customer-facing impact? any write loss or indexing delays?

maria: no writes failing to S3; ingestion write path is fine. Downstream indexing (search) is behind by ~4m which could affect recent logs in debugging for customers.

kaI: (typo) kai: I see the autoscaler CPU metric feed lagging in metrics pipeline; prometheus scrape for `ingest/hpa` went stale for ~3m due to scrape target timeouts earlier. HPA didn't see metric bump in time.

sre_oncall_alex: immediate mitigation: scale log-consumer deployment to 6 replicas manually and increase parallelism for consumers.

dave: doing `kubectl scale deploy/log-consumer -n ingest --replicas=6` now.

incident-bot: :information_source: PagerDuty PD-22183: acknowledged by alex at 1991001115.

maria: started ramping up replicas. monitoring backlog decrease.

sre_oncall_alex: after scale — checking consumer backlog and consumer lag:
```bash
# after scale
TOPIC         PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
raw-logs      0          1302000         1500000         198000
raw-logs      1          1301500         1501000         199500
```

sre_oncall_alex: lag dropping but still high. CPU on new pods currently ~45-55%, network egress stable. Seems to be working.

kai: also re-enabled prom scrape for `ingest/hpa` which was timing out. prom logs show `up` again. that should allow HPA to behave normally for future spikes.

maria: suggest adding a short-term alert silence for non-critical downstream dashboards to reduce noise while we clear the backlog.

emma: customer comms: engineering to ops — no customer-facing outage, indexes are delayed by up to 5m for newest logs. If any customers ask, say "ingestion delays for recent logs; no data loss; team is mitigating".

sre_oncall_alex: creating a runbook note for the handoff: scaled to 6 replicas, re-enabled Prom scrape, will monitor 20m windows. If lag doesn't trend down to <50k by 1991001300 escalate to infra lead.

dave: adding a short term patch to HPA threshold from 75% -> 60% for 30m to let it scale earlier during this burst. patch applied.

sre_oncall_alex: current actions summary (TL;DR):
- manual scale deployed to 6 replicas (done)
- HPA metric scrape fixes (kai) (done)
- temporary HPA target lowered to 60% for 30m (dave) (done)
- monitoring: backlog / consumer lag, pod restarts (no restarts so far)
- customer comms: low severity visible delays, no data loss (emma)

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Reminder: PagerDuty will escalate to sec_oncall in 2m if not resolved.

sre_oncall_alex: I'm going to hand off in 18m. @maria will be primary responder after I go offline. maria, can you take post-handoff watch and trigger PD escalate if lag flattens or increases again?

maria: yep I can take it. planning to watch consumer lag, HPA activity, and prom scrape health. I'll also check downstream indexing queue length.

kai: leaving a quick checklist in the thread for the handoff:
1) check kafka consumer group lag (`kafka-consumer-groups.sh`)
2) check pod CPU/replica count (`kubectl get hpa && kubectl get pods -n ingest`)
3) check prom targets for `ingest/*` (`/targets` in Prometheus)
4) if lag not improving after 30m -> scale to 8 and notify infra lead

emma: noted. I'll be on standby for customer messages.

sre_oncall_alex: handoff at 1991001200 -> maria. posting handoff summary below: "Scaled to 6 replicas, HPA fixed, lowered threshold temporarily. Lag decreasing but not yet under 50k. Watch for 20m, escalate if not improving."

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty PD-22183: acknowledged by alex, reassigned to maria at 1991001200.

maria: ack takeover. I'll keep updates here every 10m or on change.

(10m later)

maria: 1991001260: lag at ~60k per partition, trending down. No new consumer restarts. HPA showing 6->7 briefly then stable at 6.

dave: reverting HPA target back to 75% now that the spike is subsiding.

maria: 1991001320: lag below 30k and trending to normal.Closing PD?

emma: recommend waiting until <10k for confirmation, but customer comms can be updated: "Ingestion delays resolved; normal operations restored."

maria: will mark as resolved when backlog <10k. monitoring 10 more minutes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty PD-22183: resolved by maria at 1991001345.

sre_oncall_alex: great work. I'll add a follow-up ticket to investigate root cause: why prom scrape timed out, and consider smoothing HPA metrics and add a buffer for sudden batch jobs.

maria: filing follow-up: ENG-5432 "Investigate prom scrape dropout causing delayed HPA reaction -> metric smoothing + runbook updates". Assign to kai + infra.

kai: will take a look tomorrow. initial hypothesis: transient connection error to remote exporter under high load.

emma: closing note for postmortem: customer impact minimal (5-6m delays), no data loss. Ops and SRE mitigated within ~30m. recommend: brief customer note optional. :thumbsup:

sre_oncall_alex: thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:
